dimensions.gloss: Named patterns of fraudulent or improper authorship practice — buying/selling author slots, cartel-like reciprocal crediting, and denying or inflating credit.
variants: problems with or misuse of authorship

dimensions.gloss: A structural construct describing how organizational power hierarchies couple to who performs hidden (often AI-assisted) labor without credit.
dimensions.note: Singleton construct from one scheme; not clearly a disclosure field, but the closest axis available for it.

dimensions.gloss: Standard research-methodology reporting items — registration, protocol, randomization, replication, study design, results — borrowed from generic reporting guidelines and listed alongside AI-specific disclosure items.
dimensions.note: These describe generic study-reporting quality rather than AI-use/authorship/COI disclosure per se, but each scheme treats them as one checklist axis alongside its AI-specific items.

dimensions.gloss: Whether information about an AI system's pre-release testing and robustness evaluation is disclosed.
What AI operations, tools, or tasks are permitted, prohibited, gated, or delegated — often tiered by risk, role, or workflow stage before use is allowed.
variants: procurement and tool approval standards for educational uses
prohibits ai usage other than language improvement
dimensions.note: Groups governance-of-use mechanisms (bans, pre-use gates, approval standards, risk tiers, rule-specified latitude) that all answer "what AI use is allowed here," as distinct from whether disclosure itself is required.

dimensions.gloss: The recommended format for citing or attributing the resource (software or data) itself.
variants: preferred format for attributing or citing the resource itself
preferred format for citing software entries

dimensions.gloss: Whether an enforcement policy or sanctions exist for non-compliance, and whether procedural safeguards guard against biased or opaque application of those sanctions.
variants: presence of enforcement policy or sanctions for non- compliance
procedural safeguards to protect students from biased detection and opaque sanctions

dimensions.gloss: Whether reasonable alternative options are presented to support user choice and shared decision-making.

dimensions.canonical_label: Technical properties of the disclosure/authentication mechanism
dimensions.gloss: The technical qualities required or claimed of the mechanism that authenticates or labels AI content — e.g. authentication method, robustness, machine-readability, unforgeability.
The top-level domain category a scheme assigns an item to (e.g. Provenance, Rights Registries, Attribution).
dimensions.note: Classifies the taxonomy's own entities/domains rather than describing a disclosure of production; kept as its own axis since no other label matches it.

dimensions.gloss: The type of concern or harm through which an AI-authorship issue is framed (e.g. authorship fraud, misuse/overreliance, erosion of analytic labor, ethical complexity), as distinct from a risk level or tier.
High-level principles offered to guide institutional policy reflexes on AI use, rather than a measurable field of a disclosure.
How accountability or public responsibility for AI-assisted work is allocated among human and institutional parties, and whether named individuals are assigned to roles.
Whether and how privacy, confidentiality, and data security were protected when using AI (e.g. no sensitive data uploaded, redaction, access control).

Whether disclosure is backed by evidence of the underlying process — drafts, logs, portfolios, or a defensible account of the reasoning behind claims — rather than a bare declaration that AI was used.
variants: process-based explanations of how those contributions were made
dimensions.note: "Reasoning-path clarification" concerns explaining the AI system's own reasoning to a reviewer rather than a human defending their process; folded in here as a close call on the same underlying axis (disclosed reasoning/process).

dimensions.gloss: The channel or format through which disclosure-relevant information becomes observable (e.g. audit-report communication, narrative disclosure, process measures, market information).
Whether a policy or system references or aligns with external professional verification standards, international guidelines, or regulation.

dimensions.canonical_label: Profile of people involved in the dataset
dimensions.gloss: The characteristics of people involved in creating a dataset (collection team, annotator team) or represented by it (collection target).
dimensions.note: The "collection target" item describes data subjects rather than producers; grouped with the team-profile fields because all three follow the same "profile of ___" pattern from one scheme describing people connected to the data.

dimensions.gloss: The programming language associated with a software resource, recorded as descriptive metadata.
Named roles a contributor (human, or in some schemes AI) may hold in producing the work, such as project administration, revision, or a CRediT-style role list.
The specific commercial/promotional elements (discount, branded link, giveaway, slogan) present in sponsored content.
variants: promotional features mentioned in blog post

dimensions.gloss: The technical detail of how AI was used that is disclosed or logged — prompts, parameters, configuration, retrieval settings, interaction process, and the environment needed to reproduce or trace the AI-assisted step.
dimensions.note: Broad merge of many near-synonymous checklist items (logs, documentation, engineering, strategies, technique) that describe the same axis — how much of the prompt/technical interaction is disclosed. "Prompt-provenance stamp & micro-team split" is a coupled verbatim phrase whose provenance half fits here.

dimensions.gloss: A rubric level (vague to precise) judging the quality of the human-written prompt itself, distinct from whether the prompt was disclosed.
Whether a policy on prompt hygiene has been documented and communicated.
How much of the output the AI produced, or how the human/AI contribution is proportioned, including whether the human's role was limited to prompting.
variants: proportional representation of human and ai contributions

dimensions.gloss: A guiding principle that disclosure requirements should scale to the significance of the AI use (minor vs substantive) rather than apply uniformly.
variants: proportionate and technology neutral approach to ai reporting

dimensions.gloss: Whether publication of information about a new technology's price is mandatory, recommended, or not required.
variants: proposed price of the new technology
dimensions.note: The source example values ("Publication is mandatory/recommended/No publication") describe a publication mandate rather than a price, suggesting a data-extraction mismatch; canonicalized on the literal label text.

dimensions.gloss: The core facts of an AI-assisted step being recorded — which tool, what access route, what data was exposed, what humans accepted or rejected, and what verification occurred.
Whether provenance information remains attached to and available with content over time.
A legal-evidentiary doctrine prioritizing provenance credentials (e.g. C2PA) as the basis for admissibility or certification rules.
A free-text field for any other relevant information not captured by the scheme's named items.
Where a dataset/record is deposited or registered, its resolvable persistent identifier, and the date it was made publicly available.
variants: repository name(s) where the data/software are deposited

dimensions.gloss: How versions or publications relate to one another (supersedes, revises, responds-to, precedes) to preserve lineage across a document's history.
The category of venue through which something was published (peer-reviewed journal, intergovernmental/government body, private company).
Where within the document (e.g. Methods vs Acknowledgements) the AI-use disclosure statement should be placed.
variants: put the disclosure in your manuscript.

dimensions.gloss: Whether reusability metadata required by the FAIR R1/R2 criteria — clear usage license, detailed provenance, community-standards compliance, and qualified cross-references — is present.
dimensions.note: Several pairs (e.g. "R1.2" / "R1.2: Provenance") are literally the same FAIR sub-criterion labeled with and without its descriptive suffix across the software- and data-oriented versions of the same checklist.

dimensions.gloss: Instances where quality, integrity, or transparency is invoked as a general value or enacted practice rather than a specific measurable disclosure field.
dimensions.note: Deliberately distinguished from named disclosure fields elsewhere in the batch (e.g. prompt disclosure, disclosure placement) per the vague-virtue-vs-named-field test; "routines" specifically describes transparency being performed to construct trustworthiness.

dimensions.gloss: How fractional authorship credit is allocated by author rank/position, and the rationale given for that order.
Ratings of a reviewed guideline's own clarity, actionability, and assessment specificity — an evaluation of the scheme rather than of a disclosed production process.
variants: ratings of clarity, actionability, and assessment specificity

dimensions.gloss: The excuses or justifications people give for not disclosing AI use (e.g. victimless behavior, minimal contribution, responsibility denial).
A rubric criterion judging a student's subject-matter mastery in an AI-assisted assignment, unrelated to whether AI use was disclosed.
dimensions.note: An outlier content-accuracy rubric item that does not describe a disclosure axis; kept as its own dimension since nothing else in the batch matches it.

dimensions.gloss: Guidance on when in the research process authorship should be discussed among collaborators.
variants: recommendations for when to discuss authorship

dimensions.canonical_label: Intended use and scope of dataset
dimensions.gloss: The recommended uses and coverage gaps a dataset is intended to address.
Whether communication partners understand the role AI played in producing a message, named as its own axis distinct from the amount of AI contribution.
Classification of entities by type of institutional affiliation (industry vs academic/government vs unclear) relevant to conflict-of-interest assessment.
A review-level observation about how often a given kind of evidence is reported across studies, rather than a disclosure field itself.
Whether disclosed information (e.g. a conflict of interest) matches the underlying facts, distinguishing under-reporting from over-reporting.
A reference naming the checklist/guideline document itself that will be used to assess complete and transparent AI reporting, rather than a content axis of that checklist.
Whether a policy requires authors to disclose AI use at all, as a yes/no/not-stated field, distinct from what use is permitted or where disclosure goes.
variants: require authors to disclose the use of ai during submission

dimensions.canonical_label: Stage of AI use in the workflow
dimensions.gloss: The phase or stage of a workflow (research process, peer review, AI system lifecycle) at which AI was used or applicable, and the purpose tied to that stage.
variants: purposes and stages of llm integration
review stage where the ai tool was used

dimensions.gloss: The subject-matter topic of the research itself, a descriptive/meta field rather than a disclosure axis.
Whether a deliverable still depends on an opaque/black-box AI component even after disclosure or explanation is given.
variants: residual opacity in the final deliverable

dimensions.gloss: Whether/how long collected data is retained, treated as a distinct data-governance concern from privacy/security protection.
Whether AI-generated content is re-checked over time to prevent stale outputs from being silently reused.
Rights ownership (e.g. rights tokens held by rightsholders) and the separation of technical access from permission.
The risk level or tier assigned to AI-generated content or use, which governs what disclosure/labeling obligations apply.
Whether risks or safety warnings about the AI-assisted output are communicated to the end user (what could make this unsafe).
Whether a product's claimed function/role matches its documented classification (e.g. against SaMD frameworks), an audit of role-labeling accuracy.
A mechanism for translating a framework into self-assessment tailored to each stakeholder role (authors, reviewers, editors, publishers).
An operational practice of rolling self-critique loops used to manage model uncertainty during AI-assisted work.
The specific kind of task AI assistance was used for (e.g. literature search, summarizing, identifying references), as a categorical task-type axis distinct from the extent/amount of AI contribution.
